newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Hundreds homeless after fire in Ho Chi Minh City.
newsitem.headline: Hundreds homeless after fire in Ho Chi Minh City.

text.p: About 550 people were left homeless and a seven-year-old boy was killed when a fire swept through a slum in Ho Chi Minh City, local officials said on Wednesday.
The fire, which lasted for an hour, was started by flames from a kerosene cooker early on Tuesday and destroyed 99 of the Phu Tho district's many dilapidated wooden homes.
Earlier, officials had said the fire broke out on Monday night, but they had confused it with another blaze in a neighbouring district.
"My empty hands are all I have left," said Vu Minh Duong, the head of a family of seven, as he stood among charred debris where his 28 square metre (30 square foot) home had been before.
Some of the homeless were given temporary shelter at a nearby racecourse, while others had already returned to the site and erected makeshift tents.
The boy, whose age officials originally gave as five, died because he was trapped in an upper floor of one of the homes as the fire spread.

Donations of money, rice, clothes and furniture flooded in for the homeless. By midday on Wednesday, 125 million dong ($10,800) and 24 tonnes of rice had been collected. Police estimated that the fire caused damage worth one billion dong ($86,000).
